scenario.name: Mandiant UNC1945, CrowdStrike LightBasin & GSMA — Telecom GPRS Tunneling Protocol (GTP) & Roaming Interconnect Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine an international postal bridge connecting rival national carriers so travelers can receive mail abroad. An intruder posing as a friendly foreign post office requests a private sealed mailbag lane across the bridge, stuffs unauthorized internal maintenance parcels inside those sealed bags to sail straight past the outer security checkpoints, and installs a rigged front-door lock and secret hallway chute inside the telecom headquarters. In this scenario (T1133, Mandiant UNC1945, CrowdStrike LightBasin & GSMA, Telecom GPRS Tunneling Protocol , GTP & Roaming Interconnect Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: rogue PDP Context Creation Request, then encapsulated GTP-U Inner Packet Routing, then custom PAM Module. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Rogue PDP Context Creation Request, then Encapsulated GTP-U Inner Packet Routing, then Custom PAM Module, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 2123 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: Custom PAM Module (/lib64/security/pam_unix_auth.so) & iptables Covert Port Rule Audit
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1556.003 - Modify Authentication Process: Pluggable Authentication Modules)
stages.description: Inside the telecom core server room, the intruder swaps out the building’s staff badge reader for a rigged lock that accepts their secret skeleton password and cuts a hidden redirection chute in the reception desk so any call from their chosen source window slides quietly to a covert backroom listener. On the Linux/Solaris mobile core server, forensic inspection of /etc/pam.d/sshd and iptables -t nat -L PREROUTING reveals a modified PAM shared library and a covert PREROUTING port-redirection rule forwarding specific source ports to a hidden listener (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with NetfilterTable=nat PREROUTING, CovertRuleTrigger=TCP Source Port 33891 -> Local Port 55221, ThreatGroupAttribution=LightBasin , UNC1945 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes rpm -Va pam || dpkg --verify libpam-modules (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , rpm -Va pam || dpkg --verify libpam-modules via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passin so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1556.003 during "Custom PAM Module , /lib64/security/pam_unix_auth.so & iptables Covert Port Rule Audit" , On the Linux/Solaris mobile core server, forensic inspection of /etc/pam while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact iptables -t nat -L PREROUTING -n -v --line-numbers runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , iptables -t nat -L PREROUTING -n -v --line-numbers via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1556.003 during "Custom PAM Module , /lib64/security/pam_unix_auth.so & iptables Covert Port Rule Audit" , On the Linux/Solaris mobile core server, forensic inspection of /etc/pam while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --sport 33891 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 55221 / ⇠#3 ACK 59) from Node ③ (#3 GTP Border Firewall (:2123/:2152)) to Node ④ (#4 SGSN / GGSN / MME Core Node), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 HLR / HSS Subscriber Database).

steps.simpleExplanation: On the Linux/Solaris mobile core server, forensic inspection of /etc/pam.d/sshd and iptables -t nat -L PREROUTING reveals a modified PAM shared library and a covert PREROUTING port-redirection rule forwarding specific source ports to a hidden listener (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with NetfilterTable=nat PREROUTING, CovertRuleTrigger=TCP Source Port 33891 -> Local Port 55221, ThreatGroupAttribution=LightBasin , UNC1945 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
